title: Vakratunda Mahakaya — Ganesha invocation
textOriginal:
वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय सूर्यकोटि समप्रभ ।
निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा ॥
transliteration:
vakratuṇḍa mahākāya sūryakoṭi samaprabha |
nirvighnaṃ kuru me deva sarvakāryeṣu sarvadā ||
meaning: O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty body, radiant as ten million suns: make all my undertakings free of obstacles, always.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Traditional Gaṇeśa invocation verse (popular prayer; no single canonical scriptural locus identified in the sources). Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. shlokam.org matches word for word (writes "sūryakoṭi samaprabha"). title: Om Namah Shivaya — Panchakshara mantra
meaning: "Om, salutation to Śiva" — the five-syllable (na-maḥ-śi-vā-ya) mantra of Śiva, with the sacred syllable Om.
sourceText: Panchakshara mantra; root in Sri Rudram (Taittiriya Samhita 4.5.8)
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Pañcākṣara mantra; Vedic root in Śrī Rudram (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5.8, Rudram anuvāka 8): "namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca". "ॐ नमः शिवाय" copied from the mantra line in sanskritdocuments Rudra Panchakam. Vedic locus confirmed on sanskritdocuments Rudram (vinā-svara) at anuvāka 8.1: "नमः शिवाय च शिवतराय च" and in the svara-sahita Rudram (anuvāka 8). The Rudram line itself has no "ॐ"; the Om-prefixed five-syllable form is the traditional japa form. The Rudram nyāsa on the same page also says "नमः शिवायेति बीजम्". IAST generated mechanically from the Devanagari.

title: Karpura Gauram — Shiva dhyana
textOriginal:
कर्पूरगौरं करुणावतारं
संसारसारं भुजगेन्द्रहारम् ।
सदा वसन्तं हृदयारविन्दे
भवं भवानीसहितं नमामि ॥
transliteration:
karpūragauraṃ karuṇāvatāraṃ
saṃsārasāraṃ bhujagendrahāram |
sadā vasantaṃ hṛdayāravinde
bhavaṃ bhavānīsahitaṃ namāmi ||
meaning: I bow to Bhava (Śiva), white as camphor, compassion incarnate, the essence of worldly existence, garlanded with the king of serpents, ever dwelling in the lotus of the heart, together with Bhavānī.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Traditional Śiva dhyāna/ārati verse (commonly said to be from the Yajurveda tradition; no canonical locus confirmed in the fetched sources). Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. shlokam.org agrees (writes "संसारसारम्" and "सदावसन्तं" joined; same reading). Variant: sanskritdocuments Rudra Panchakam reads "सदा रमन्तं" ("always delighting") instead of "सदा वसन्तं" ("always dwelling"); the vasantaṃ reading is the one in both other sources. The source verse has a danda only after lines 2 and 4, reproduced as-is.

title: Shantakaram — Vishnu dhyana
textOriginal:
शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं
विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् ।
लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं
वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥
transliteration:
śāntākāraṃ bhujagaśayanaṃ padmanābhaṃ sureśaṃ
viśvādhāraṃ gaganasadṛśaṃ meghavarṇaṃ śubhāṅgam |
lakṣmīkāntaṃ kamalanayanaṃ yogibhirdhyānagamyaṃ
vande viṣṇuṃ bhavabhayaharaṃ sarvalokaikanātham ||
meaning: I worship Viṣṇu, the peaceful one who reclines on the serpent, lotus-navelled lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast as the sky, cloud-dark and beautiful of form; Lakṣmī's beloved, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation, remover of the fear of worldly existence, sole lord of all worlds.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review

Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. No substantive variants.

title: Hare Rama Hare Krishna — Maha-mantra
textOriginal:
हरे राम हरे राम राम राम हरे हरे ।
हरे कृष्ण हरे कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण हरे हरे ॥
transliteration:
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare |
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare ||
meaning: An invocation of the divine names Hari, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, sixteen names in all; the Upaniṣad teaches that chanting them removes the defects of the Kali age.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Kali-Santaraṇa Upaniṣad (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda), section 2. Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. The Upaniṣad gives the "Hare Rāma" half FIRST. Wikipedia confirms this order and notes that the popular order (Hare Kṛṣṇa first, as sung by ISKCON/Gauḍīya tradition following Caitanya) reverses the two lines. If the temple uses the popular order, swap the two lines; do not alter the words.

title: Sri Rama Rama Rameti — Rama nama
textOriginal:
श्रीरामरामरामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
सहस्रनामतत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥
transliteration:
śrīrāmarāmarāmeti rame rāme manorame |
sahasranāmatattulyaṃ rāmanāma varānane ||
meaning: Śiva tells Pārvatī: "O fair-faced one, I delight in Rāma, the delightful, by repeating Rāma, Rāma; the one name of Rāma is equal to the thousand names (of Viṣṇu)."
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Viṣṇu Sahasranāma (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva), uttara-pīṭhikā / phala-śruti, verse 27 (Īśvara uvāca). Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. stotranidhi (IAST) matches: "śrīrāma rāma rāmēti ramē rāmē manōramē | sahasranāma tattulyaṁ rāma nāma varānanē || 27 ||". Source prints an alternative reading "(रामरामेति रामेति)" for the first pāda, removed from the text and recorded here. Popular recitation often spaces it "श्रीराम राम रामेति".

title: Ugram Viram — Narasimha mantra
textOriginal:
उग्रं वीरं महाविष्णुं
ज्वलन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् ।
नृसिंहं भीषणं भद्रं
मृत्युमृत्युं नमाम्यहम् ॥
transliteration:
ugraṃ vīraṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ
jvalantaṃ sarvatomukham |
nṛsiṃhaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhadraṃ
mṛtyumṛtyuṃ namāmyaham ||
meaning: I bow to Nṛsiṃha, the fierce and heroic Great Viṣṇu, blazing and facing every direction; terrifying yet auspicious, the death of Death itself.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review
notes: Source detail: Nṛsiṃha Mantrarāja (anuṣṭubh), expounded pada by pada in the Nṛsiṃha Pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad (Atharvaveda). Devanagari copied from bhaktibharat (sanskritdocuments has no clean contiguous copy of the verse). Cross-checked word by word against the Nṛsiṃha-tāpanīya Upaniṣad on sanskritdocuments, which lists the eleven padas: उग्रं, वीरं, महाविष्णुं, ज्वलन्तं, सर्वतोमुखं, नृसिंहं, भीषणं, भद्रं, मृत्युमृत्युं, नमामि, अहम् — all match. title: Sarva Mangala Mangalye — Devi stuti
textOriginal:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ।
शरण्ये त्र्यम्बके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
transliteration:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike |
śaraṇye tryambake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te ||
meaning: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O gracious Śivā who fulfils every aim, O refuge, three-eyed Gaurī — Nārāyaṇī, salutations to you.

title: Ya Devi Sarvabhuteshu — Devi stuti
textOriginal:
या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥
transliteration:
yā devī sarvabhūteṣu śaktirūpeṇa saṃsthitā |
namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
meaning: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings in the form of power (śakti): salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, again and again.

title: Namastestu Mahamaye — Mahalakshmi Ashtakam
textOriginal:
नमस्तेऽस्तु महामाये श्रीपीठे सुरपूजिते ।
शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ते महालक्ष्मि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
transliteration:
namaste'stu mahāmāye śrīpīṭhe surapūjite |
śaṅkhacakragadāhaste mahālakṣmi namo'stu te ||
meaning: Salutations to you, O Great Māyā, seated on the throne of prosperity, worshipped by the gods; O Mahālakṣmī, holding conch, discus and mace, salutations to you.

meaning: "Om, (salutation to) the one born in the Śaravaṇa reed-pond" — the six-syllable (śa-ra-va-ṇa-bha-va) mantra of Murugan/Skanda.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review

title: Japa Kusuma — Surya (Navagraha Stotram)
textOriginal:
जपाकुसुमसंकाशं काश्यपेयं महाद्युतिम् ।
तमोऽरिं सर्वपापघ्नं प्रणतोऽस्मि दिवाकरम् ॥
transliteration:
japākusumasaṃkāśaṃ kāśyapeyaṃ mahādyutim |
tamo'riṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ praṇato'smi divākaram ||
meaning: I bow to the Sun, the maker of day, red as the hibiscus flower, son of Kaśyapa, of great brilliance, the enemy of darkness and destroyer of all sins.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review

title: Gange cha Yamune — sacred rivers
textOriginal:
गङ्गे च यमुने चैव गोदावरि सरस्वति ।
नर्मदे सिन्धु कावेरि जलेऽस्मिन् संनिधिं कुरु ॥
transliteration:
gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati |
narmade sindhu kāveri jale'smin saṃnidhiṃ kuru ||
meaning: O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu and Kāverī — be present in this water.
checkedBy: Fetched from source and cross-checked against a second source (automated extraction, 2026-09-28); awaiting CNESS editor review

title: Dvadasha Jyotirlinga Smaranam
textOriginal:
सौराष्ट्रे सोमनाथं च श्रीशैले मल्लिकार्जुनम् ।
उज्जयिन्यां महाकालमोङ्कारममलेश्वरम् ॥
परल्यां वैद्यनाथं च डाकिन्यां भीमशङ्करम् ।
सेतुबन्धे तु रामेशं नागेशं दारुकावने ॥
वाराणस्यां तु विश्वेशं त्र्यम्बकं गौतमीतटे ।
हिमालये तु केदारं घुश्मेशं च शिवालये ॥
एतानि ज्योतिर्लिङ्गानि सायं प्रातः पठेन्नरः ।
सप्तजन्मकृतं पापं स्मरणेन विनश्यति ॥
transliteration:
saurāṣṭre somanāthaṃ ca śrīśaile mallikārjunam |
ujjayinyāṃ mahākālamoṅkāramamaleśvaram ||
paralyāṃ vaidyanāthaṃ ca ḍākinyāṃ bhīmaśaṅkaram |
setubandhe tu rāmeśaṃ nāgeśaṃ dārukāvane ||
vārāṇasyāṃ tu viśveśaṃ tryambakaṃ gautamītaṭe |
himālaye tu kedāraṃ ghuśmeśaṃ ca śivālaye ||
etāni jyotirliṅgāni sāyaṃ prātaḥ paṭhennaraḥ |
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ smaraṇena vinaśyati ||
meaning: A remembrance of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna at Śrīśaila, Mahākāla at Ujjayinī, Amaleśvara at Oṃkāra, Vaidyanātha at Paralī, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, Nāgeśa in Dārukāvana, Viśveśa at Vārāṇasī, Tryambaka on the Gautamī, Kedāra in the Himālaya, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya. Whoever recites these names morning and evening is freed of the sins of seven births.
